run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T07:46:11Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy fired because 500s generated in the checkout path propagated out through frontend to frontend-proxy: frontend-proxy's own ingress (server) and "router frontend egress" (client) spans turn STATUS_CODE_ERROR from 0 to ~0.44-0.49 spans/s each from 07:47Z, carrying error=true and http.status_code=500. One fully visible failing trace shows the chain load-generator POST 500 -> frontend-proxy ingress 500 -> frontend POST /api/checkout 500 -> frontend grpc CheckoutService/PlaceOrder rpc 13 -> checkout PlaceOrder 13 -> checkout HTTP POST (5.004697 s, error) -> shipping /get-quote (5.001423 s, "Internal Server Error") -> shipping "POST quote" client span (5.001365 s, "Timeout"). shipping's client-side p95 for "POST quote" rose from 39-70 ms before 07:46Z to 9.4-9.7 s during the incident, while the destination quote service's own POST /getquote server p95 stayed flat at ~1.9 ms with no error-status spans and successful "Calculated quote" log lines. Kubernetes events in otel-demo record PodNetworkChaos controller updates for exactly the quote pod (quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w) and the shipping pod (shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv) starting 2026-11-15T07:46:05Z and repeating at :00/:05 each minute through 07:55:05Z, six seconds before the alert's start and just before the first non-zero error-rate point (07:47:11Z). All pods were Running with 0 restarts (started 07:09Z), all deployments 1/1 ready on image demo:2.1.3, all nodes Ready, and the quote Service/Endpoints and shipping QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080 were consistent, so application error, misconfiguration, restart/OOM and rollout causes were checked and rejected; the deepest cause the evidence supports is a pod-level network fault on the shipping<->quote path.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span error rate was 0 before 07:47Z, became 0.0778 spans/s at 07:47:11Z, plateaued at 0.89-0.97 spans/s from 07:53:11Z to 07:59:11Z and returned to 0 at 08:03:11Z; the same error count is split between span_name="ingress" and span_name="router frontend egress" (~0.44-0.49 spans/s each) while STATUS_CODE_UNSET traffic stayed ~18-21 spans/s.

Broken down by span kind, frontend-proxy SPAN_KIND_SERVER error spans went from ~0-0.019 spans/s before 07:47Z to 0.489 spans/s at 07:55:11Z, and SPAN_KIND_CLIENT error spans from 0 to 0.481 spans/s, i.e. both the nginx/Envoy server side and the egress-to-frontend client side of frontend-proxy recorded errors.

In traces returned for shipping error spans (07:50-07:52Z), frontend-proxy spans "ingress" and "router frontend egress" appear with status tags error=true and http.status_code="500", alongside frontend POST /api/checkout 500, load-generator POST 500, checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder rpc.grpc.status_code=13, and shipping "/get-quote" and "POST quote" spans with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR.

Whole trace a9079927020859300f7ba10e2e121cc3 (load-generator user_checkout_multi) shows the propagation order and durations: frontend-proxy ingress 500 (5.044093 s) -> router frontend egress 500 (5.044021 s) -> frontend POST 500 -> POST /api/checkout 500 -> executing api route /api/checkout 500 -> frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder rpc 13 (5.041958 s) -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder rpc 13 -> checkout HTTP POST error (5.004697 s) -> shipping /get-quote error "Internal Server Error" (5.001423 s) -> shipping "POST quote" error "Timeout" (5.001365 s); no span of the quote service is present under shipping's "POST quote" span in this trace.

The exact error text propagated upward is otel.status_description/exception.message "shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500" on checkout's PlaceOrder span and on frontend's "executing api route (pages) /api/checkout" span (grpc status 13), while shipping's own failing child span is named "POST quote" with status description "Timeout".

shipping's "POST quote" client-span p95 latency was 39-70 ms at every point from 07:25:11Z to 07:47:11Z and then jumped to 9400-9725 ms at every point from 07:49:11Z to 08:01:11Z (same query window, comparable in-window baseline).

The quote service's own POST /getquote server-span p95 latency stayed at 1.90-1.98 ms across the whole window including the incident (no latency change), and the span metrics returned for quote (POST /getquote, calculate-quote, {closure}) contain only STATUS_CODE_UNSET series, no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series.

quote and email span rates fell from ~0.55-0.6 spans/s before the incident to ~0.085-0.096 spans/s from 07:49Z onward, the same relative drop as checkout's successful oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder rate (0.559 spans/s to 0.085-0.096 spans/s), so the lower inbound rate at quote tracks the reduced end-to-end checkout throughput rather than an observed quote-side failure.

quote pod logs (container quote, current instance) show a continuous stream of "Calculated quote" lines up to 2026-11-15T07:46:03Z, after which they appear only in short bursts of roughly 5-8 lines at 07:47:00, 07:48:00, 07:49:00, 07:50:00, 07:51:00, 07:52:00, 07:53:00, 07:54:00, 07:55:00 and 07:56:00.

Kubernetes events in namespace otel-demo show controller status events (reason Updated, message "Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource") for involvedObject PodNetworkChaos/quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w and PodNetworkChaos/shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv at 07:46:05Z, then at :00 and :05 of every minute from 07:47 to 07:55; these two pods are the only involved objects returned for the namespace, and the first such event precedes the alert start (07:46:11Z) by 6 seconds.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running and ready with restart count 0, including shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv (start 07:09:22Z, IP 100.96.1.109), quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w (start 07:09:23Z, IP 100.96.1.165) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-wvxht (start 07:09:22Z); every deployment reported readyReplicas=availableReplicas=updatedReplicas=1 on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-<service>, so there was no restart, reschedule or rollout inside the incident window.

The quote Service (selector opentelemetry.io/name=quote, port 8080->8080) resolves to endpoint 100.96.1.165:8080, the quote pod's IP, and the shipping deployment's container env sets QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080, so shipping's quote destination name and the quote Service/Endpoints were consistent.

All five cluster nodes report only condition Ready=True, with no MemoryPressure, DiskPressure or other pressure condition set to True, including i-0b4b26fa385533a10 which hosts quote, shipping, frontend-proxy, payment, product-catalog, accounting, fraud-detection and flagd.

Error-status span series in the window were returned only for accounting, ad, checkout, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, payment, recommendation and shipping; accounting and payment stayed at 0 error spans/s throughout, ad, fraud-detection and recommendation stayed at ~0.0037 spans/s or 0, while checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and shipping rose together from ~07:47Z and returned to 0 at 08:03:11Z.

A complete trace sampled at 07:51:04Z shows a successful request through the same path during the incident: quote POST /getquote 316 us, shipping /get-quote 2061 us, shipping "POST quote" 1930 us, checkout PlaceOrder 101 ms with rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and email POST /send_order_confirmation returning http.status_code=200 in 5448 us.

Counter-evidence against a quote application failure: quote's own spans stayed fast (p95 ~1.9 ms) and carried no error status, its pod logged successful "Calculated quote" lines, and a 07:51:04Z trace shows quote answering in 316 us, so the failing hop is the shipping->quote call, not quote's handler.

The 20 newest frontend-proxy traces returned for 06:46:11-08:03:59Z (spans starting 07:57:40.865719Z-07:57:43.484849Z) contain no error-tagged span: all 31 "ingress" and 32 "router frontend egress" rows carry http.status_code 200 (27/28) or 308 (4/4), so that particular biased trace sample alone does not exhibit the failures the span metrics record at the same minute.

Most likely cause: a pod-level network fault was applied to the shipping and quote pods. PodNetworkChaos controller events for exactly those two pods begin at 07:46:05Z, six seconds before the alert's start, while shipping's client-side "POST quote" p95 goes from tens of milliseconds to ~9.7 s, quote's server side stays at ~1.9 ms with no errors, and shipping logs a 5.0 s "Timeout"; this is consistent with requests/response packets between the two pods being delayed or dropped rather than with either application failing.

Open question on the exact fault direction: the evidence does not distinguish a fault on shipping egress, on quote ingress, or a bidirectional fault between the two pods; both pods carry PodNetworkChaos objects, and no span reveals which direction was affected.

Second candidate not fully excluded: the propagated message "failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500" could point to the email hop. In the same failing trace the failing client span is shipping's "POST quote" (Timeout) and no email span is a child of shipping, while no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series existed for email and the sampled intra-incident email POST /send_order_confirmation returned 200; the referent of the "email service" wording therefore remains unverified rather than confirmed.

Rejected: quote service application degradation or quote-side errors as the cause. quote's POST /getquote p95 was unchanged at 1.9-1.98 ms, quote's span metrics contain no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series, and a 07:51:04Z trace shows quote returning in 316 us.

Rejected: quote Service/Endpoints misconfiguration or a wrong destination address. The quote Service selects opentelemetry.io/name=quote on port 8080 and has endpoint 100.96.1.165:8080 (the quote pod), and shipping's QUOTE_ADDR is http://quote:8080.

Rejected: pod crash, OOMKill, eviction or resource-exhaustion as the cause. Every otel-demo pod was Running/ready with restart count 0, no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff events were returned in the namespace (only the PodNetworkChaos status events), and all nodes were Ready without pressure conditions.

Rejected: a deployment rollout or image change at 07:46Z. The shipping, quote and frontend-proxy pods all started at 07:09:22-07:09:24Z, every deployment shows ready=available=updated=1, and all service images are ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-<service>, i.e. unchanged demo 2.1.3 images.

Rejected: node-level failure. All five nodes were Ready with no pressure conditions, and on the node hosting quote and shipping (i-0b4b26fa385533a10) the unrelated payment and accounting services kept zero error spans throughout while only the shipping->quote checkout path failed.

Inspect the PodNetworkChaos objects (and their parent network-chaos rule) for quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w and shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv to confirm the injected fault's direction, selector and duration, and identify who applied them; the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the origin of the fault could not be verified.

Review the shipping service's outbound HTTP client settings and error strings: the failing call to QUOTE_ADDR is reported as "failed POST to email service" even though the trace's failing child span is "POST quote" to the quote service, and a 5 s timeout/retry produced ~9.7 s p95 per checkout.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules returned status no_data both for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and for an unfiltered listing, so the exact expression, threshold and 1-minute evaluation that produced the annotation value "current: 0.6444444444444444" are unknown, and that value could not be reproduced (measured frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR share of server spans peaked near 0.489/(0.489+9.493) ~ 4.9%).

The PodNetworkChaos objects themselves are not readable with the available tools (their kind is not in the permitted kind list) and enumerating CRDs failed with RESULT_TOO_LARGE, so the fault type (loss, delay, partition), the direction, the duration and the API group of PodNetworkChaos are unknown; only the controller status events for the two pods were observed.

The change_history data source is not integrated, so who or what created the network-chaos objects and when exactly the fault was removed could not be verified; the last observed chaos status event is 07:55:05Z and the 5-minute error-rate windows decay to 0 by 08:03:11Z.
No NetworkPolicy objects were returned for otel-demo (query status no_data, not an observed empty set), so a policy-based cause could be neither confirmed nor excluded from that source.

The email container produced no readable log lines in 07:44-08:00Z (bytes_read 0, status no_data), so email-side behaviour could not be checked from logs; the propagated text "failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500" remains unexplained against the trace, which shows the failing hop as shipping -> quote.

Trace data is a biased, incomplete sample (traces_search reported incomplete and capped at the requested trace count), so no complete call graph or failure rate is claimed; the 20 newest frontend-proxy traces at 07:57:40-07:57:43Z contained no error spans even though span metrics show errors in that minute.

Request volume and 5-minute rate averages shifted during the incident because each failing checkout blocked for ~10 s, so error and request rates during the plateau are not directly comparable to the pre-incident throughput.
next_steps: Read the NetworkChaos/PodNetworkChaos specifications for the quote and shipping pods to record the fault direction, parameters and schedule, and compare with the 07:46:05Z start and the ~07:55Z last status update.
Confirm with the change/chaos tooling (not integrated here) who applied the network fault at 07:46:05Z and whether it was intentional.
Correct the shipping service's dependency label in its failure message so a quote-service timeout is not reported as an email-service failure.
Verify the RequestErrorRate alert rule expression and threshold in Prometheus so the reported 0.6444 value can be tied to a specific metric selector.
